name: Dent Disease 2

criteria.description: Presence of low-molecular-weight proteinuria confirmed by urine protein electrophoresis or immunoassay
Elevated urinary calcium excretion above age-adjusted normal limits
Absence of pathogenic variants in CLCN5 gene with identification of pathogenic variants in OCRL gene
Evidence of progressive decline in renal function leading to chronic kidney disease
Family history consistent with X-linked inheritance pattern

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of low-molecular-weight proteinuria and hypercalciuria plus identification of pathogenic OCRL gene mutation or exclusion of CLCN5 mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential to distinguish Dent Disease 2 from Dent Disease 1.

common.symptomName: Fatigue related to chronic kidney disease
searchTerms: fatigue linked to chronic kidney failure
low energy due to kidney problems
bone deformities from vitamin D deficiency

rare.notes: Reported in some patients with OCRL mutations

laboratory: Low-molecular-weight proteinuria (e.g., elevated beta-2 microglobulin or retinol-binding protein)
Elevated serum creatinine in progressive stages
imaging: Renal ultrasound showing nephrocalcinosis or nephrolithiasis
Bone X-rays indicating rickets or osteomalacia
genetic: Absence of pathogenic variants in CLCN5 gene
other: Family history consistent with X-linked inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of pathogenic variants in CLCN5 gene
Similar clinical presentation but genetically distinct
Generalized proximal tubular dysfunction with multiple solute losses
Often associated with systemic diseases or drug toxicity
Proteinuria due to other renal tubular disorders or systemic diseases
Lack of hypercalciuria or genetic confirmation

redFlags: Rapidly progressive renal failure in a young male
Family history of X-linked renal tubular disease
references: Lloyd SE, Pearce SH, Fisher SE, et al. A common molecular basis for three inherited kidney stone diseases. Nature. 1996.
Hoopes RR Jr, Shrimpton AE, Knohl SJ, et al. Dent disease with mutations in OCRL1. Am J Hum Genet. 2005.
